How do people from many cultures make one country together?
immigrant. A person who moves to a new country to live there. Example: Maya Lin's parents were immigrants from China.
immigration. Moving to a new country to live.
heritage. The culture and traditions passed down to you from your family.
citizen. A member of a country, with rights and duties. People born in Puerto Rico are U.S. citizens.
diverse. Made up of many different kinds of people or things.
detain. To hold someone and not let them leave. Many immigrants were detained at Angel Island.
E pluribus unum. Latin words on U.S. coins. They mean "Out of many, one."
An immigrant moves to a new country to live. People come to the United States for many reasons. Some come for jobs or school. Some come to be safe, or to join family.

I ask: did everyone come by choice? No! Indigenous Peoples were here first, for thousands of years. Many Africans were taken from their homes and brought here against their will. They were forced into slavery. Immigrants chose to come. So America's story has many different beginnings.

A push makes people leave home, like war, hunger or no jobs. A pull draws people to a new place, like jobs, safety or family. Example: In the 1840s, potato crops failed in Ireland. Many people went hungry. That was a push. Jobs in American cities were a pull. Over a million Irish people came.
Each group brings its culture : foods, music, languages and holidays. Families pass down traditions. Many traditions mix and become shared American ones. This makes the country diverse .

Let me look at a bowl of gumbo , a Louisiana soup. Okra came from Africa. The word gumbo comes from an African word for okra. Filé, a spice made from ground leaves, came from the Choctaw people. The roux, a cooked flour sauce, came from French cooks. One bowl holds many cultures!

Lucía's family makes tamales every Christmas Eve. Her grandma learned to make them in Mexico. Now Lucía helps fold the corn husks. Is this a tradition? Yes! It is passed down, and they do it again and again. It is part of Lucía's heritage .

U.S. coins say E pluribus unum . That is Latin for "Out of many, one." People from many cultures make one country. But newcomers were not always treated fairly. People worked to change unfair laws, just like in Week 13.

Let me test the motto with facts. In 1882, a law kept out most workers from China. Was that "out of many, one"? No. It was unfair. In 1943, that law ended. In 1965, a new law treated people from all over the world more fairly. The country did not always live up to its motto, but people pushed it closer.

Can you be fully American and keep your family's culture? Yes! Sonia Sotomayor's family came from Puerto Rico. She speaks English and Spanish. She is a justice on the U.S. Supreme Court. Many Americans are proud of two cultures at once. Out of many, one!

Source 1, a poem. Emma Lazarus wrote The New Colossus in 1883. In 1903, it was put on a plaque inside the Statue of Liberty. Part of it says: Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free. Word help: huddled masses means big crowds pressed close together. Yearning means wanting very much. Source 2, a law. The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 said most workers from China could not come to the United States. Many Chinese people who did come were detained at Angel Island for weeks or even months. Some carved poems in Chinese into the wooden walls. The law ended in 1943.

Sonia Sotomayor. She grew up in the Bronx in New York City. Her parents came from Puerto Rico. People born in Puerto Rico are U.S. citizens , so they moved but did not immigrate. She loved Nancy Drew books. In 2009, she became the first Latina justice on the U.S. Supreme Court. She writes picture books for kids too.

Maya Lin. Her parents moved from China to the United States. She grew up in Athens, Ohio. At age 21, she was still in college. That year, she won a contest to design the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C. It is a long black stone wall. It holds the names of more than 58,000 Americans who died in that war. She also designed the Civil Rights Memorial in Alabama.

Yo-Yo Ma. He was born in Paris, France, to parents from China. His family moved to New York when he was about 7. At age 7, he played the cello for President John F. Kennedy. He started the Silkroad , a group that mixes music from many cultures. He plays music from all over the world.
